questions_and_answers.question: To plan for retirement, Eric deposits $288 each quarter in an annuity that pays 7% interest, compounded quarterly. Payments will be made at the end of each quarter. Find the total value of the annuity in 27 years.
questions_and_answers.answer: To find the total value of the annuity in 27 years, we need to use the formula for the future value of an annuity: FV = P * ((1 + r)^n - 1) / r where: FV is the future value of the annuity P is the periodic payment (in this case, $288) r is the interest rate per period (in this case, 7% / 4 = 1.75%) n is the total number of periods (in this case, 27 years * 4 quarters per year = 108 quarters) Substituting the values, we get: FV = 288 * ((1 + 0.0175)^108 - 1) / 0.0175 FV = $144,536.77 Therefore, the total value of the annuity in 27 years will be $144,536.77.

questions_and_answers.question: To plan for retirement, Hans deposits $331 each quarter in an annuity that pays 7% interest, compounded quarterly. Payments will be made at the end of each quarter. Find the total value of the annuity in 25 years.
questions_and_answers.answer: Answer To calculate the future value of an annuity, we can use the formula for the future value of an ordinary annuity: FV = P * [(1 + r/n)^(nt) - 1] / (r/n) Where: FV is the future value of the annuity P is the amount deposited each period r is the annual interest rate (in decimal form) n is the number of times interest is compounded per year t is the number of years In this case, Hans is depositing $331 each quarter (so P = 331), the interest rate is 7% or 0.07 (so r = 0.07), interest is compounded quarterly (so n = 4), and the annuity is for 25 years (so t = 25). Substituting these values into the formula, we get: FV = 331 * [(1 + 0.07/4)^(4*25) - 1] / (0.07/4) You can calculate this expression using a calculator to find the future value of the annuity.
